claims.text: The two groups show distinct attacker behaviors that can be directly compared using the visible facts.

In Group 1 (source 183.62.140.253) each request targets a different invalid username, uses separate source ports (33521 and 33902), and is followed by an immediate “Received disconnect … Bye Bye [preauth]” line that terminates the session before any successful authentication attempt occurs.

In Group 2 (source 187.141.143.180) every request attempts to log in as **root**, uses three distinct source ports (33314, 34508, 35685), and also ends with the same “Received disconnect … Bye Bye [preauth]” line after each failed password attempt.

Both groups share the identical pre‑authentication disconnect pattern, but Group 2’s repeated targeting of a privileged account (root) combined with its higher request cadence (three attempts within 11 seconds) makes it more anomalous relative to typical brute‑force noise.

Root‑cause hypothesis: the attacker in Group 2 is likely an automated script that systematically probes for default or weak credentials on administrative accounts, while the activity from Group 1 appears to be a less focused enumeration of random usernames, possibly part of a broader reconnaissance sweep.
